summary.intent: Add shift-left defect checks to three plugin agent definitions (vector:challenger, canon:auditor, lambda:implementer), then bring references, docs, versions and marketplaces current and ship. The session later shifted to auditing the wider plugin ecosystem and polishing the companion HTML design artifact for desktop and mobile.
summary.outcome: The three agent edits shipped as commit b87105e: two new shared references, version bumps (vector 1.5.0, canon 2.2.0, lambda 1.6.0, ecosystem 3.4.0), changelogs and READMEs, pushed and pulled into the marketplace cache. The needs_architecture routing in lambda's SKILL.md was closed. The artifact was reworked through rendering-based fixes (SVG collisions, font sizes, mobile overflow). Overflow is now zero from 320 to 1920px, but sticky nav and the ecosystem audit punch list are still unresolved.

repo: Editable source is /Users/gabe/Projects/agent-plugins. ~/.claude/plugins/marketplaces/orin-dx-agent-plugins is a separate checkout that only updates via push then pull, so edits never reach it automatically.

The auditor agent lives at plugins/canon/agents/auditor.md, not audit-spec.md. The audit-spec name is a skill (plugins/canon/skills/audit-spec/SKILL.md). The file already had six dimensions before the edit, so the new one made seven, contradicting the user's '6th' framing.

Agents follow a five-part tag structure (constitution, backstory, goal, judgment, output) plus an optional <load_first> block that scanner/reviewer use to load shared/references/*.md. New cross-cutting checks should be sourced from a shared reference, not restated inline.
canon/gate-spec writes gated specs to <workspace_root>/.claude/specs/<id>.json. auditor.md never said so, which was a latent gap for scope-overlap as well as the new boundary-round-trip dimension.

Repo validation scripts: scripts/check-versions.sh, check-mermaid.sh, check-skills-doc.sh, check-reference-size.sh (120-line cap per reference). Docs must follow shared/references/docs-voice.md and conventional-commits.md.
Two marketplace manifests exist: root marketplace.json (AGY schema, carries per-plugin versions) and .claude-plugin/marketplace.json (Claude Code schema, no per-plugin versions by design).

The hazard taxonomy T1-T10 is a load-bearing contract referenced by proof:scanner, proof's SKILL.md and the -t7-t10 companion files. Adding an 11th entry would touch files outside the original scope, which is why a standalone reference was chosen.
Precedent for adding a review or audit dimension is a minor bump (canon 2.0.0 to 2.1.0). Cross-plugin batches use the 'ecosystem' commit scope.

Subagent audits found delta's receive-feedback SKILL.md and README claim must-fix/suggestion/question triage that review-preprocessor does not implement and whose <judgment> forbids. Basis's scaffolder and auditor mandate exactly five sections, so they cannot generate or recognise <load_first>.

code.finding: <judgment> says NEVER make judgments about change quality. This contradicts the must-fix/suggestion/question categorization advertised in delta's receive-feedback SKILL.md and README.
Mandates exactly five sections in order with no optional <load_first>, so scaffolded agents can never include the convention that 5+ real agents use.
Literal check for exactly five sections would fail or ignore agents that carry <load_first>, and it does not verify that a needed <load_first> exists.

workflow: Render and inspect pixels (playwright via npx, screenshots, crops, pixel sampling) instead of reasoning from CSS or markup. The SVG label collisions and mobile overflow were only found once this started.
Test responsive layouts at many widths, including breakpoint boundaries, not just desktop. Measuring scrollWidth minus clientWidth at 20 widths found overflow that spot checks missed.

CSS grid items need min-width:0, otherwise min-content from wide tables or long unbreakable <code> strings inflates tracks and the whole page. SVGs set to width:100% shrink their text illegibly on phones, so give diagrams a min-width floor and a scroll container.
The Artifact read tool returns platform-wrapped HTML. Editing and republishing that file embeds Anthropic's wrapper markup, so strip it to clean body content before editing.
Parallel background subagent audits were a cheap way to sweep the plugins not yet touched, each inheriting the failure patterns found so far.
Confirm before pushing or committing outward-facing changes, and keep the request's scope tight. Versioning and changelog work was initially held back as out of scope until the user asked for it.

friction: User had to push back repeatedly on the artifact's header, spacing, color and diagram text size before real rendering was used. Several rounds relied on unverified CSS reasoning.
The hero decoration was tuned three times before being cut. The color retune left one old bright hex behind because of an indentation mismatch in the edit match.
The artifact source being edited was the platform-wrapped render, so wrapper pollution was republished several times before being noticed.
Mobile and tablet overflow (296px at 375px, 92px at 768px) went uncaught because testing used only 1400px, and breakpoint-edge overflow at 901 and 980px surfaced only on a later sweep.
The user was unaware of the open items and asked why they hadn't been surfaced earlier. The initial brief's '6th dimension' and registry 'five dimensions' counts were stale versus the actual files.
Some AskUserQuestion prompts were interrupted by the user.
open_items: Add sticky section navigation to the artifact: sidebar on desktop, horizontal scroll pill strip on mobile, no hamburger. The user has not yet confirmed.
Consider importing from the reference artifact: a hero verdict box, inline confidence tags, rationed callouts, tabular-nums on numeric table columns.
Decide how to resolve delta's receive-feedback vs review-preprocessor mismatch: add real triage logic or narrow the docs.
Basis scaffolder and auditor need to learn <load_first> as an optional section and check for it.
Subagent audits of graph+trace and axiom+proof were launched and their results were not seen in the transcript. The basis findings were truncated.
Out of scope by user choice: the two-gate human checkpoint protocol and loop-back automation (proof to architect on recurrence of 2 or more, periodic drift-checker/audit-backlog runs).
The 'context hygiene' detail (only the pre-scan's structured output enters challenger's context) was offered as an optional challenger.md line and not confirmed.
The cached agent-registry description of canon:auditor still says 'five dimensions' and lives outside the repo.
